item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 12
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil season 1 episode 12. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

This episode started from the previous end, that Tanya was sad that the Empire stopped defeating the navies of the Republic. She went to the strategy room, and wanted to talk to the General Zettour or other top brass. But they were out because they celebrated the armistice. She was disappointed and tried to leave the building but Rerugen found her and invited her to his office. He asked her to talk frankly, and she said something. I think she warned that the temporary short victory would backfire when the war would start. But he didn't understand why she thought the war would continue. And she explained to him that the Empire's strategists were too logical and smart, so they didn't account for people's emotional nature. That was a little bit surprise to me to hear because she was also a logical woman, but it made sense that her experience in this life and in the previous life made her think they were sometimes emotional. He was surprised and no word to that.

But then, Tanya was totally right. The Republic declared the war in the Southern continent in the next month, and Empire's citizens and soldiers were upset. Even people started feeling the war never ends. Well, for more than 10 years, definitely they would feel that way, especially lives didn't get better. Kurt and Zettour were also upset. I don't know what they thought and whether they remembered what Tanya had tried to do, but maybe they regretted it. Zettour's guess was completely correct that the other superpower would join the war and there were still 2 giant powers so I don't know what would happen to the story.

Because the location of the Republic's navy was in the different continent, the Empire couldn't move many of soldiers. And 203rd battalion went to the continent and the Tanya spoke in front of her battalion. Well, basically, she hated the Being X so much she demonstrated it in front of them.

On the other hand, Mary, the daughter of the Major in the Entente Alliance, went to the US and volunteered to join its military. Obviously, she was also possessed by the Being X, and this was going to be the boss in the season 2.

Anyhow, that was the end of the episode. The earlier parts, there were a few comedies but Tanya was good. The later episodes in this season focused mainly on the war and great to think. The audio for rifles, artillery, and tanks are good, and the animation didn't move much but sometimes moved well. I remembered this was great, and still this was good at this age.

Watched 2nd time. It totally made sense from Rerugen's point of view, Tanya looked a monster. She was like 10 years old, and she started saying a history and how she felt from her personal experiences for how people's nature was. And then her guess was right and the war continued. From his perspective, she was unimaginable and hard to believe, so totally made sense he believed she was a monster of a little girl form.

This episode was mostly an epilogue to the previous episodes and a prologue to the next season.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 11
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil season 1 episode 11. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

This episode started repeating the end of last episode. And then started fighting against the Allied Kingdom. They had long range weapons, and also their battalion was bigger than the 203rd of Tanya's. Because of it, some of them were shot down and they needed to fight in a difficult battle. Tanya noticed they couldn't leave because they would've been going to shot down from behind if they had done it and the reinforcement would take more than 10 minutes. So they must've fought there alone. Audios were great as always, and the animation were more than great. The camera works in the airforce battle with rifles were dynamic and moved around 360. Also, the movement of Tanya was different from other soldiers and she sometimes suddenly moved upside down and shot down rear enemies. Then she noticed there was a large cloud and escaped there to wait for enemies and attacked. But the Colonel of the Allied Kingdom was also strong, and seemed he had a weapon, track weapon or something, which wasn't allowed in a treaty and he still used it. Tanya and Visha were trying to fight and avoid the attack, but he was able to catch up and it seemed it was so hard to fight them. It was great, that Tanya's power of the God's blessing still didn't easily defeat enemies neither. She used that power only to protect the Weiss, who was trying to attack the Allied Kingdom's Colonel who shot down some Tanya's soldiers. Anyway, he persistently chased and attacked Tanya, and in the end, they faced to face, and then started brawl battle instead of a rifle. Tanya's brawl is still strong enough though she was a kid, but the Colonel was possessed by Being X, so he was trying to blow himself up. Visha stopped it once and she had a chance to take a distance from him but he anyway exploded and she got damaged. Because the Colonel was dead and the reinforcement of the Empire came to the sky, the Allied Kingdom left.

Then, the soldiers shot by them, including Grantz, were actually survived and gathered again. So, they were temporarily invalidated but they would still be able to fight? What the hell?

Then, the next scene was after 15 days, and the Empires' military marched into the capital of the Republic. Apparently, they stopped fighting afterward and took the Republic, and many people announced or thought it was the end of the war. 203rd battalion's mens went to a beach in the Republic and took a vacation, as if it was an operation. Well, they were definitely men. Visha and Tanya were in a still their military building, but then Tanya noticed the Republic didn't give up completely. As far as I've understood, they had navies and fled to the another country so they would be able to counter attack.

Tanya was trying to do anything she can to stop it, but anyone didn't want to, her boss, Visha, and one from HQ commander, and she needed to stop. She was so upset and angry that another operation would really end the way but she couldn't. Well, that would backfire for them for sure. It's obvious that the Empire will be attacked from multiple directions, the Allied Kingdom and the Republic, at the same time.

Let's see what'll happen. This episode was still very good especially the Colonel was really like a boss here for Tanya.

Watched 2nd time. Alright. Trench gun was violated by a treaty in this world, but it seemed it was not in a real. The Colonel's purpose was to revenge by any means to Tanya, so he didn't care that. And the last shot he got was from the gun his daughter gave to. How sad was it.

Then the Empire was satisfied with armistice and Tanya must stop by the top priority's order from a command HQ. It was very stupid from the point of Tanya and us, but it was obvious that nobody didn't experience a World War in this country, so they left them freely. Also, they won the Rhine too well that they underestimated the risk. Only Tanya who knew the World Wars knew what would come to them by this decision. That made sense because Being X stalked her so they were going to attack her. That was sad.

Anyhow, that was the end of the episode.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 10
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil season 1 episode 10. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

So this episode started from the operation Tanya started in the previous episode. I thought the Republicans noticed when they arrived but they didn't, so it was a mission to keep themselves hidden and attacked Republic's communications HQ. Well, because the V-1 flew way higher than most people fly so they couldn't detect nor notice them. And Tanya and Visha killed soldiers like assassins and brought down the one building, but it was empty. Tanya wanted to check the status from others but they didn't respond. It was great that she looked upset for this critical mission. But it was successful on both groups after a couple of attempts and they left the HQs.

Then Zettour and Kurt were blamed by any other people in a meeting room and they demanded explanations. Well, it kinda made sense that they wanted to know the plan because the military only said it'll be gone. Then the news came and they were surprised, but Zettour had really a bold heart.

Then there was another operation in the west side of the Rhine and it succeeded. I was like, if they were able to do it, why did they need Tanya's operation. But it seemed it was the most effective way to bring down the Republic and couldn't have been used because it was only target to the west side. So the Empire was now surrounding the Republic's forces that were attacking into the Empire. This was a good war anime to see.

The 203rd battalion was in a submarine. I was like, why were they there? But apparently, they planned to surround the Republic like mages so they couldn't leave the battlefield. But before arriving the battlefield, Grantz was shot and went down. I wasn't sure he was going to be out. I mean, I expect Tanya would lose many of her soldiers for sure, but maybe not this time and for him? Anyhow, they were attacked by the Allied Kingdom led by the man who was defeated in the Entente Alliance. He was for the vengeance, but if it was for vengeance, then why didn't he shoot Tanya at first? I had no idea what they thought.

Watched again. Okay, I missed a lot of parts. First, no wonder the Republic's HQ didn't notice 203rd's groups. They attacked partially to make them busy. And then, submarine was prepared so they can leave the place.

And then the Operation Lock Pick was prepared for an entire year. I thought why no Republican soldier or even people noticed it, but probably they were too busy on the war line and didn't care a little far place of the underground.

When Tanya knew the operation Lock Pick was successful and ordered to join the operation Revolving Door, she looks happier than other times. And also, when she flew and was thinking about the peace time, I really felt she was a regular person who didn't want to join a war.

And then, the man from Entente Alliance. How could he become Colonel in the Allied Kingdom? That was a little weird thing, but probably Being X was involved.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 9
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil season 1 episode 9. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

After the last episode, Tanya thought about the strategy in Arena City. And she thought she didn't get her hands dirty. I thought she was more of a criminal-minded person so it was unexpectedly different.

Then the HQ had a plan in the Rhine theater. They retreated from there, got the Republic to move forward into the Empire's domain, and then attacked them. That was risky, and they were very nervous.

So in the day, the 203rd battalion fought in the Rhine. And they tried to retreat, and Tanya disobeyed the order not to make retreat look deliberate from enemies at that time. Afterward, the Grantz and Visha were in a tent for injured, and it was a contrast that they were laughing each other while another patient was in a dire strait.

Then they've heard the grand strategy. And what they relied on was the invention from the crazy Engineer. Maybe that person was the one she was scared the most. And they needed to rely on the one-way experimental flying steel objects.

Tanya also shared the strategy to the 203rd battalion without hesitation. Weiss and even Grantz were worrying about themselves, because the success heavily relied on them. However, Visha had nerves of steel and slept right before that day and they relieved seeing her. How could she be so tough, or did she think Tanya was that dependable? And it's not even the soldiers in the battalion. Even Zettour and another top brass were even nervous during the dinner and it was silent. That was a kinda real and sure that proposal was a life or death one.

And in that day, they used the flying plane with a catapult. In the plane, Tanya was thinking how come she got the most dangerous place in the world even though she wanted to be in rear. Well, it was obvious that she was trying to be brave to Zettour and couldn't turn down his offer. It would've been different if she had been. But instead, she had thought it was by the Being X. Well, it could be partially true, though, without it, she didn't have the... What was its name? The Type 97? and couldn't win that many battles.

Anyway, this episode was more for preparation and the next one was going to be important.

Watched this episode on the 2nd time.

Tanya met Uger who she thought he dropped from the career ladder in a military in a few episodes ago. However, he became a Major and worked in a rear with Zettour. So apparently, he got a job exactly what Tanya wanted. She should learn from him and follow it, but somehow didn't follow and just talked.

In the Rhine, the 203rd battalion was fighting but the fight was rough. It was good that this was not like other Isekai anime, that MCs are very strong and can defeat enemies without any sufferings.

Visha and Grantz talked, and she knew he had something in his mind, so she thought he was suffering from what he did in the Arena City. So, she talked about what they learned in a school and said that was an order from Tanya and an actions' responsibility was from the commander. Well, Tanya was well aware about that, but she probably thought it was by the Commander's responsibility.

Also, Rerugen seemed not to be scared to Tanya and even tried to salute her. I thought he was a person who kept doubting her and would be an important role to make her fail. It looks it's not.

V-1's abilities to move surprisingly fast, just going straight, and only one way usage toward the death place sounded really familiar to me. It was because 86 had the same episodes, so stories with Sci-Fi or modern wars tend to have these inventions.

At the end, Tanya needed to write a letter because one soldier left her battalion. But she lost them because they ate a rotten potato. It was obvious in the Rhine theater, there was not enough food and soldiers were desperate.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 8
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil season 1 episode 8. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

There was a rebellion in the Arcane City and Republic also joined, and the 203rd battalion must invade the city. So unlike previous 2 episodes, the enemy wasn't weak nor was the attack a surprise. When they attack with a common sense, it was going to be rough because the battlefield will be in a city, and there were civilians in the battlefield. Besides, republic soldiers were there. Tanya was ordered to eliminate the Republic and the rebel from an upper commander but he also wondered why people wanted to become soldiers. The thing was, theoretically speaking, under the international law, anyone who remained in the city after the fight was declared counted as a Republican soldier, which sounds merciless.

Then Tanya went to the city and got snipers. They were split and also prepared to fight with artillery, snipers, and mages. Mages were also dexterous and were able to protect attacks from Tanya's battalion. But Tanya was able to push them back to disable artillery as well. Then she declared the surrender and release their custody of the Empire soldiers. They didn't accept and even shot someone who tried to flee from the rebel. Visha took the picture, and the HQ decided to take down the entire town, so the entire town burned down and killed civilians, too, mercilessly. They saved their soldiers, though.

Then the first lieutenant was trying to stop Tanya when she was trying to shoot artillery with fleeing civilians, but she attacked him and in the end, she ordered him to shoot them down. He saw one kid with vengeance and he was trying to leave the city, and made up his mind and shot them. That was really, the Tanya the Devil.

After this way, there was a talk between Zettour and Rerugen. And the point was, the basics of this strategy, and the hole of the law, was found out and proposed by Tanya and Zettour decided to pick her brain for the Empire. This man is really a mastermind of the Empire, for sure.

Watched again.

So I overlooked it, but the Arcane city was originally in the Republic, so there were many civilians who were originally from the Republic, and that's the reason why the Republic's commander Bouttene? tried to escape them.

This story showed each character well, the main point of view was second lieutenant Grantz. He seemed to enjoy the war in the Rhine on the early episode, and tried to earn his stripes somehow, probably by the number of soldiers he eliminated. However, right after he heard from the Tanya for the Arcane, he started bothering and said his words aloud, then afterward, he even tried to disobey Tanya. So if this was not a war, he would be a positive, outward, sociable, and great man. On the other hand, the first lieutenant Weiss was the person who always warned Grantz to be careful and ask to follow orders. He looked he was a good soldier, but he got a shot and needed to leave the battlefield. Tanya looked through him that he was hesitant to shoot enemies in the city because he was thinking too much. So, he was a person who thought a lot, looked around and took care of others, but didn't show that if it's an order usually. Visha, however, seemed not to struggle. This woman was scary to Tanya for sure, but other than, she was kinda non-emotional in a war. She obviously knew what was going to happen, but she recorded when the Empire's custody soldier fled to the Command, and the command to wipe out the city started, and she didn't change her face a little. Or maybe she followed Tanya too much. However, the normal soldiers shooting by artillery guns had the strongest mind because they knew what would happen and still fired because it was from an upper order.

Tanya obviously knew, that the command was the one she originally proposed and top brass took that proposal and used it. So maybe she was happy not to take reckless operations and didn't have to risk her life, and also that was efficient from her perspective. However, could the 203rd battalion catch up with her? I kinda felt they will eventually betray her, or at least some of them and there are plenty of reasons to do. Well, that's more like how much Tanya could earn trust points from her subordinates so they thought she can be trusted.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 7
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil season 1 episode 7. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

This episode was no comedy but drama. At first, the story began from the point of Major in the Entente alliance. He said goodbye to his daughter, Mary, and wife because they left a city, and he got a christmas gift from Mary. That was a submachine gun, and he wore it.

Then, the PoV was changed to Tanya. She was trying to disagree with a plan of her high commander, who was trying to put full force into the Norden line despite her concerns of exhaustion and supplies. She even showed her dissatisfaction through her behavior, like pouring milk into her coffee messily and spilling it over her desk. Then she talked to 2 other high ranks, one of them was Rerugen, and talked about the benefits of full force to the Norden line, and correctly guessed what the true purpose of this attack of the Empire was. They planned to use that attack as a decoy and attack from the rear as a surprise attack. She was a logical employee in her previous life, so she was trying to find a rational answer behind the intent of the tactics, but Rerugen at least couldn't believe she was able to figure out this plan by herself. Because of this, or maybe planned from the beginning, 203rd battalion joined the campaign.

Tanya didn't like it, and she even had a backup plan for retreat in case she and the first lieutenant died. She didn't even empathize with her own people, but she was logical to think about these things too. Then they started attacks on the rear of the Entente Alliance, the fjord city or something. Their plan was to destroy all cannons in the port so battleships were able to come closer to the port, but the major of the Entente Alliance couldn't figure it out. And he had them destroy all of them. Tanya even took a risk to fight one battalion with one company, but her company somehow managed to defeat them. The major was actually the person who fought her in the Norden line in the 2nd episode, and he remembered her. So he was trying to take her down, but right before she killed him off, her battalion destroyed all canons. So instead of fighting, she decided to leave the city. Well, it was a little bit dangerous for her not to attack that major in front of her, because he could attack her, wasn't it? Maybe she was confident she could block his attacks completely. Anyhow, the Empire's battleships came, and the Entente Alliance couldn't stop them at all, so the battle was over, but the major didn't stop and tried to defeat Tanya. Of course, he couldn't do it and Tanya killed him. Then she found out his submachine gun was good, and decided to get it as her christmas gift. That's the difference between a normal person who got a present from his daughter, with a wish that she wanted her father back, and the so-called Devil Tanya, who got whatever she thought was useful. It wasn't that cruel as it was a war, after all.

Then the top brass of the Empire was glad of the success of this fight. But the Mary and her mother were crying in a place, who left from that city before it was attacked.

Watched 2nd time.

The BGMs when Tanya started attacking the Orse Fjord and left on a ship were probably ones for Tanya or the Empire, but they sounded like a boss BGM. On the other hand, the one for the major of the Entente Alliance, who was determined to attack Tanya, was like the important scene where a main character attacks. Throughout this anime, the Tanya was drawn as an evil for sure.

Tanya still had the mind of an employee and cared about her career, whether she lost her job, or could go back without overwork, on a battlefield. Well, technically, that might be right, but it sounded so wrong when you faced the life and death battle.

Also, it's obvious that the 203rd battalion is so strong and each of them could block attacks from others and didn't have any casualty in the Fjord, compared to the Alliance's battalion, who couldn't block the attacks except the major. That was a reason why she could defeat the battalion with a company.

If the Entente Alliance had more people in the city like the major had said, the result would've been different considering how long they took to break down cannons.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 6
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 6. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

So unlike the previous episode, this episode was pretty serious. The HQ in the Empire needed the 203rd battalion to go to the Norden, and Tanya left. And she also predicted there were some other countries intercepting the Empire, like the Republic. And also she guessed Being X was involved.

Then they went to the Norden, and fighting against the enemies. Tanya thought reinforcements were not necessary and fought enemies with her battalion and the existing one. And she even said that the least achieving person needed to pay for the whole battalion, was it really a war? But she also tried to pull her weight there. Well how heavy was that weight?

Enemies were not only mages, but also bombers that flew at 10,000 altitude. Tanya fought them back, but it was true that the bombers might attack other planes if Tanya went up, and she also easily eliminated the commander's plane. It was interesting that bombers dropped their remaining bombs to make themselves lighter and flee faster. But she was able to use her T-97 or something to target multiple planes like some kind of robot.

Then she met Being X and they tried to make her face an entire world as an enemy. Well, Tanya was right. Being X isn't really God. It's a devil or some sort, from what they said to Tanya. Then she also tried to eliminate the enemy's observers from a distance. They had a rumor about Tanya, but they thought that was a myth. Yeah, nobody wanted to believe a kid used monstrous magic.

It seemed to me that she was really enjoying a war and also is willing to fight against an entire world if she can take down Being X. So, she is, from one aspect, definitely an evil.

After the ending, Tanya went to a commanding operation room, and she was worrying about 2nd hand smoke. It was funny that all of those officers smoked in front of the kid who was 10 years old or so, and her face looked like she really hated it.

Watched 2nd time.

A commander of the Allied Kingdom on the observation team was actually excellent, and they noticed when Tanya attacked them even though his subordinates questioned what she was trying to do. And they shortly noticed she tracked their techs.

Also, despite what she wanted, Tanya really was suited to fight at the front because she was really obsessed with Being X and wanted to fight against the world.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 5. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

It was funny that Tanya never talked what she really wanted to anyone and other people also tried to do what she didn't want them to do. Visha was a very capable assistant that she made the team got up to speed but Tanya really want to make team setup delayed. She even did the same interview with Zuttour and got extra time for trainings. She asked only a short amount of time and Zuttor allowed, but other people didn't believe that a training can be only done in a month. Well, she obviously failed to do expectation management.

She was then tried to do some crazy trainings. At first did 36 hours to avoid bullets from the skys in a plain snow area. Then without taking rest, reaching to a target point at 48 hours. Avalanche even happened and some people were knocked down but she saved them. Somehow, that made them realize they should follow her. Well, it's like a hell training, but I guess in a war, extra rough situations can happen, so her training might be good. And because of that, applicants impressed and followed her. Maybe they underestimated Tanya because well she was a kid, and then she noticed she was tough but at least kind enough to save their lives from avalanche. In the first place, how did she do? Magic? Anyway, she got what didn't want to.

Then Rerugen came to her and gave the order, and they started a war to Davian. Davian somehow didn't have air forces and didn't encrypt communications. Well, encrypting communications sound like in WW2 to me, so may make sense, but no airforce sounded weird even to them. But they were able to exterminate Davian's army and they were able to attack their capital. Before attacking a capital for their buildings, I guess weapon factories, they needed to declare an attack to civilians because of an international law, and she declared it, with her child voice. Well, considering her age, that was natural, but even her subordinates thought she was acting and enemies didn't think that was the real communications.

Anyway, it felt weird that that country didn't have airforces. Maybe some kinds of traps? But we'll see what happens. This might trigger a war against them.

Watched 2nd time.

It was still funny she regretted she didn't make Visha to send pillbox in the Rhine. But she was good to throw a question to Tanya. In the Rhine, Tanya even didn't accept questions and always order. Despite that, she also asked questions or requests something to others like Zuttour or Rerugen. She seemed to have a double standard, or maybe she stopped doing it.

I didn't notice but Tanya's right leg was not flesh anymore and used an artificial one. It was probably gone when she was in the Nordan line so at that time, she really cost her life. Of course she didn't want to avoid the dangerous places like front lines. Well, but somehow, in a war with Dakian, she was more than happy and aggressive to attack to its capital.

She intentionally changed her voice when she declared an attack but when other people said to her that she learned acting, she wasn't really happy. Wasn't she intentional lol

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 4
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 4. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

This might be the most peaceful episode for Tanya. Tanya studied in a university for a half year. She answered a use case in the university perfectly in a class. Well, she was just an employee in a company in her past life, how could she know these things? Or was that easy enough to learn in a half year? In a day, she took care of a rifle in the afternoon while others were out in the classroom, and from other people, she was someone who really wanted to go back to the front lines and wanted to fight, which was exactly the opposite of what she wanted.

Anyhow, she just enjoyed staying there for a half year and learned, and then she happened to meet a man from a top brass. He invited her in his room and had a chat. Then he casually asked her for what a country should do in the war. At that time, it was 1924, so the war seemed to have been going on for 10 years or more. Then she brought up a chance to become a global war, perhaps from her past life knowledge, and she proposed to avoid losses as much as possible. She thought that was amazing insight and proposal, but that top brass thought she didn't want to win. Then she thought she failed to propose what she said. Anyway, because she didn't want to give the impression of unwillingness to the war, she counter argued that it'd be helpful to build a battalion to attack them. Was that battalion the idea from the WW2? Don't know. Then she thought she made a speech really good, but later, she noticed she completely messed up. That man proposed to the militaries to build a rapid-response battalion and asked her to lead. She couldn't reject it well because she was the person who never say she wouldn't, but that's a problem that everyone thought she was aggressive and loved the front line. She had a communication issue as she never told what she really wanted. What's funny was almost everyone thought she was just a kid and treated her like a kid, except Lieutenant Colonel, Rerugen, if I'm not mistaken, so if she wasn't in a war line, her mistake was somewhat acceptable. Also, Rerugen observed a person pretty well and looked through each person, apparently.

Anyhow, Tanya needed to lead a batallion, but she didn't want to, so she wanted to delay going to the war line in an upcoming global war, and was trying to delay hiring, but applications were too many. So she decided to do something, but then Visha came. It seems Visha still respected Tanya in some ways. Well, look it from her way, Tanya was so young and defeated a company in the Rhine theater and also arranged for her to come to the capital, so she was a respectable person for sure.

Watched 2nd time.

So this story was that Tanya proposed and caused to start the world war and probably fight across many countries. I don't know until which point Tanya will go in this series. What she suggested was what Zettour originally wanted so that was probably the reason why he accepted her proposal too.

She also was fighting to Being X, but how could she win against it? What was an end game? Being X can take over anybody's bodies as far as I've seen, so that means unless Tanya would exterminate everyone else, she couldn't win. Or did it actually exist in a real form and she could fight?

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 3
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 3. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

So, this episode solved my question I had in the episode 1. It started that Tanya was about to move to the science department in a lab. But she was trying not to make bad impressions that she didn't want to come back to the front line to her boss, so she showed she reluctantly accepted it. Well, that obviously caused a miscommunication, I guess, because it was so indirect.

Then she tested the jewel with 4 synchronization of something which was a new technology and still immature, and that jewel exploded not only once but also a couple of times. So she hated being a guinea pig, well mainly because that chief engineer talked about theory and not practice, and obviously didn't test at all, and except her, they couldn't test I guess. So, in the end, she ended up asking to stop the testing for the device, moving to the front line. It was approved. I think this actually gave a wrong impression to top brass that she loved front lines instead of rear and that was the reason why she started fighting in front more. I guess what the right course of action had been that she asked different tests which was from a different person, because obviously the chief engineer didn't care the safety and blamed others.

Anyway, next, the Being X came to her and talked to her with a puppet. Actually, it was able to take over not only creatures but also non organics too. They obviously failed to make her have a faith, so they started intercepting more. Then, the chief engineer started new experiment because of Being X's interception and she was about to be exploded, and obviously she knew that it was due to Being X. But she unconsciously prayed the God and used the device without any dangers. Magic? No idea. Something controlled by the Being X. But because of this, she always prayed to God to have the control of jewel, which allowed her to use more powers for magic. And this was the reason why she prayed in the 1st episode. Of course, she was atheist, but was also rational and in order to have better power, she prayed. That caused other people to believe the God, or Being X more, ironically.

Then Visha got from her to get back to the capital because of the achievement she made. Obviously, it was from Tanya, and she remembered how two other men ended up by her order so she was scared but also surprised with what Tanya gave to her. Tanya didn't laugh or react anything about the question that Visha asked whether she went to the pillbox which was target by artillery. This was because Tanya couldn't empathize with others, and maybe she thought she was treating Visha properly.

Anyway, Tanya also went back to a university and thought she was able to spend a safe life there. But Lieutenant Colonel taught others that Tanya was a monster in the little form of a girl, and some people thought she was a good soldier, so they didn't think she wanted to be in a rear but in a front, and she wouldn't be in the rear for a long for sure.

Watched 2nd time.

One of an engineer said that I didn't think this would actually work. Hey, convince your chief engineer to make it safer for testing.

Also, Tanya now got the jewel, T-95 or something, which was cursed by Being X and when she prayed the God, she was able to gain the power.

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 1
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 1. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

This anime was mainly for a war similar to the World War 1, and the Empire was from Germany, and the Republic was from France. But as it's a fantasy, there is a unit who can use a magic and they can even fly and use a magic power into a gun.

The main character Tanya Degurechaff was in the Empire side. The episode 1 started from the trench warfare of the west line in the Empire. The first, it showed how cruel the front line was and some soldiers were depressed due to the trench and some soldiers were dead. They even called there a living hell.

In the Tanya's unit, some soldiers had come to the front to fight and didn't even obey the order of the commander Tanya. Obviously, they didn't like her. She tried to dismiss them, but they didn't follow that either, so she ordered them to move to a rear. Well, obviously, she liked rules, orders, and didn't like exceptions, motivations, etc. She was like half as tall as other soldiers, so she was really a kid.

In the another day, Visha, who was one in the Tanya's unit, was exhausted and couldn't follow Tanya while flying to the front line. Tanya found out she was behind and gave her harsh words that she should leave or catch up then Visha followed catching up. Later, using Visha's exhaustion as an excuse, Tanya tried to ask the commander to avoid the fight. But Visha volunteered and insisted she was able to fight despite what Tanya said. So Visha was serious, and one who is a patriot, obviously.

Then Tanya decided to take out a Republic company, the 105th, iirc. That company had defeated the Empire's magic soldiers a lot so they underestimated any of them. But Tanya dodges any attacks, tried to take down its commander and failed, but still did so for some soldiers, and then fly to the 10,000 meters, which Republican's couldn't do. In order to fly high, I guess they should at least have the ability to deal with an atmospheric pressure, able to breathe with low oxygen, and deal with cold temperature, I guess. I guess breathe and temperature aren't usually a problem for these stories so I assume they were also able to deal with them by their magics. So, Republican's couldn't fly because of the atmospheric pressure. Then Tanya used telepathy to ask soldiers to surrender, and obviously they didn't, so she used some strong magic that could blow the entire company out. It was not as strong as an atomic bomb, but obviously it was way stronger than the normal bombs or guns and can kill not only by the explosions but also by carbon dioxide. Even Visha and others need to protect from the explosion's impact.

Some person even called her the Devil of the Rhine, not only from the enemies but also from within. And then Visha found out that Tanya ordered two men to go to the rear because they were going to be dead and Visha was scared about it. Well, she was definitely an intimidating girl for sure.

Watched again.

I noticed, this episode started that Tanya was like a fairy in the battle field, from what Visha thought, then ended that she was the monster in the form of a little girl. That was a great contrast in one episode. And also, it was 1924, so the war may continue for 10 years, assuming it had started 1914.

Also, I forgot, the Tanya didn't like the God at all. But her spell included a lot of the "praying to God" or whatever. Was she herself here? Or maybe not?

Also, the sound of the guns like artillery, rifle, or the sound of hitting them into the ground were great and real. They did a good job here. The animation of Tanya's big spell she casted when she was over 10,000 meters were, instead of visual effects from natures, they're more like mechanical with a lot of gears. That might be because she isn't natural at all.

Anyway, here is what I thought in the episode 1.
